findings.text: the added np.testing.assert_array_equal(wall_shadow, expected_wall) takes its expected side from operator._carrier_shadow_read(physical, masks, topology), the same production helper that nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:3751 calls, so both sides move together under any regression inside that helper; and the regression it claims to guard is invisible on this fixture, because the removed rule's band (|z| > 0.31 + hysteresis) and the carrier band (|z| > 0.31) select the same nodes of the 92-node wall, whose z values are 0.68*sin(k*2pi/96) plus the inserted -0.31/-0.46 segment, with no node in the 0.011 m sliver, so reinstating the height rule leaves the assertion green. The deletion is durable through the code being gone, not through this assertion.

the brief's first measure is `grep -rn wall_height nova/ tests/ benchmarks/` returning nothing at head; at head it exits 0 with two hits, this line and :436, so the measure as written is unmet. The hits are the persisted wall vertical coordinate rather than the removed rule, and renaming them was tried and reverted because the committed docs/figures/mast-centroid-capability/*/panel-fields.npz states read that key (coordinate-negative-parent.log shows the KeyError a rename produces), so the intent holds; what is wrong is that the closing artefact symbol-absence-final.log reports SCAN_EXIT=1 at revision e2d9e1d81, a superseded commit where the key was still renamed, and never describes the landed tree a reader will check.

shadow is assigned the same array as private, so the census now records shadowed_wall_node_count and private_wall_node_count, and shadowed_private_nodes_below_x_point and private_wall_nodes_below_x_point, as the same measured numbers under two names and prints them as two columns of the report table; a reader takes two agreeing columns for corroboration when the audit is now measuring one mask once. Either report the topological mask alone or keep the positive control as the single observable.
